questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid yellow arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
It means drivers may turn in the direction the arrow shows.
It tells drivers that a green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same thing as a yellow traffic light. When you see a solid yellow arrow, slow down and get ready for a red light.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done enough.
You must wait for police to arrive.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You may leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:

options.text: Flat.
Curvy.
In the sun.
In the shade.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the shade.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded roads. Areas blocked by trees or buildings freeze faster than other parts of the road and take longer to dry.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs show that you are in a school zone. Stay alert for children and pedestrians when driving near a school.

questions.question: When driving to an area you do not know, you should:

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you start driving.
Only know generally where your destination is.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance before driving to an unfamiliar area. Check a map to find your destination before you leave.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown (35 mph).
A divided highway is starting. Slow down to the safe speed shown (35 mph).
Merge ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown (35 mph).
The road winds ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown (35 mph).

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown (35 mph).
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves right and shows the safe speed for that curve (35 mph). Slow down when you see this sign.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines down the center. You may cross these lines:

options.text: Only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
To pass other cars if no traffic is coming the other way.
Never.
Only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You may only cross these lines to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the car to go.
Away from the skid direction.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the car to go.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want it to go. Once the car starts to straighten, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell you to slow down. When a new speed limit is shown on this sign, that speed limit begins at the sign.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean passing is not allowed.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
The condition of your brakes.
The condition and type of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed.

questions.question: If your car with Anti-Lock Brakes starts to lose grip on a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press hard on the brake pedal, hold it, and steer away from danger. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) pumps the brakes automatically faster than you can. If you release pressure or pump the brakes, you will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
May no longer turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction, but you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You should drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: Conditions are not perfect.
You see a police car.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when the road is wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions less than perfect. You can get a ticket for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are at the posted speed limit.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car?

options.text: Your seat belt.
The steering wheel.
Your rearview mirror.
Your seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat.
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first to get a comfortable position and clear view of the road. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel.

questions.question: When a bus is signaling to return to the main road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to return to traffic after stopping. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely re-enter traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn you about hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful where children are present. They may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes left, glance:

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in your stopping distance?

options.text: Steering ability.
Braking distance.
Reaction distance.
Perception time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with speed and road conditions.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: Only where a yield sign is present.
Only when you want to yield.
When they are working in construction zones.
When their car is bigger than yours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When they are working in construction zones.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all workers and vehicles in highway construction zones. Drive slowly and carefully through work zones.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: You may turn right at a red light after stopping and yielding, unless a sign says otherwise.
You may make a U-turn anywhere unless a sign prohibits it.
You may turn left into any clear lane as long as no cars are in your way.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn right at a red light after stopping and yielding, unless a sign says otherwise.
questions.explanation: You may turn right at a steady red light after stopping and yielding to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, unless a sign prohibits it. You may also turn left from a one-way street onto another one-way street at a red light after stopping and yielding.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles when using a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop for you.
Use crosswalks only if they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a nearby vehicle may not have time to stop.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Rely on your mirrors.
Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Other vehicles are often hidden in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet ahead on residential streets or 5 seconds ahead on freeways.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look, then go if traffic is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand downward, they are signaling that they will stop. Adjust your driving if you see this signal.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow arrow?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns in the direction of the arrow. However, oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.

options.text: White
Blue
Green
Orange

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually white with black markings. These signs control traffic and must always be obeyed.
